expect: verdict: "delete"|"class": 2|"class": 3|"asked": false|NOT:"repair": "set-upstream"
note: the three answers a branch can get, side by side: proven landed, no proof, and one that never goes whatever the proof says

expect: usable: false|the base could not be read|NOT:"verdict": "delete"|NOT:"class": 2
note: a base that does not resolve makes every merge question UNKNOWN, which is not "nothing is merged" — nothing is deleted on a reading that could not be taken

expect: usable: false|the base could not be read|NOT:"verdict": "delete"
note: no base named at all lands in the same place, and by the same rule rather than a second one written for it

expect: does not take `ahead-behind`|"verdict": "delete"
note: a git older than 2.41 answers no such field, so containment is measured one branch at a time — the fallback is a path, not a refusal

expect: it has uncommitted or untracked changes|"dirty": true
note: `worktree list` never mentions modified or untracked files, so without a status per worktree a removable one cannot be told from one holding work

expect: its working tree could not be read|"dirty": null
note: a status that would not read is not a clean tree, and the difference is a worktree somebody still has work in

expect: it holds a submodule|"submodules": true
note: a line without a leading `-` is a populated submodule, and removing the worktree takes whatever history its git directory holds

expect: it holds a submodule|"modulesDir": true
note: a `modules` directory in the admin dir is the other half of the same answer: no line at all AND no directory is the only combination meaning nothing is there

expect: proof: "forge"|"verdict": "delete"
note: a squash leaves no ref-level proof, so only the forge knows the branch landed — and where its merge landed is what settles it

expect: that merge is not in the base|NOT:"proof": "forge"
note: a merged request whose merge commit the base does not carry landed somewhere else, and that is a surface rather than a delete

expect: where it landed cannot be read here
note: an object this repository does not have makes the containment check die rather than answer no — unknown, which is not unmerged

expect: a change request on its tip is still open|"verdict": "keep"
note: an open request keeps the branch whatever else matched: what a reviewer asks for next has nowhere to land without it

expect: answered: false|the forge did not answer for this tip|NOT:"proof": "forge"
note: a forge that did not reply makes the sweep NARROWER, never wider — a squash-merged branch it cannot see stays standing

expect: may hold the only copy|"repair": "unset-upstream"|"verdict": "delete"
note: `[gone]` is the upstream's own state and not a proof of anything: gone AND merged is a delete, gone and unmerged may be the only copy left

expect: answered: true|"proof": "forge"
note: the host this repository actually lives on, read from its own url — a self-hosted instance asked of the SaaS answers about somebody else, or about nothing

expect: read: false|could not list this repository's worktrees
note: a listing that failed classifies nothing, rather than answering with no worktrees

expect: read: false|could not list this repository's branches
note: the same on the other half: no branches read is not a repository without branches

expect: not inside a git checkout
note: a call with no repository under it is a call this cannot act on at all

expect: needs --default
note: a ref to read and a name to compare are two values, and neither is the other trimmed

expect: is not owner/name
note: a repository that is not owner/name would steer the request somewhere else

expect: unknown argument '--everything'
note: a mistyped flag silently ignored would answer about a question nobody asked

expect: it is checked out in a worktree|NOT:"verdict": "delete"
note: a branch checked out anywhere stays, and git says the same — `branch -D` refuses one another worktree holds. Whether that worktree goes in this run is not this script's to know

expect: a branch name this cannot read was skipped|NOT:"verdict": "delete"
note: a value that would steer a ref never reaches one, and being skipped is said out loud rather than leaving the branch quietly unmentioned

expect: repair: "set-upstream"
note: the default branch points at the base, and the comparison is ref against ref — `origin/master` against `refs/remotes/origin/master` never matches, and the tracking then gets "repaired" on every run
